title: Inference path hedging runbook — regional slab guidance
body:
Purpose:
This working runbook synthesizes a set of spreadsheet-ready heuristics and scenario cells for modeling per-request unit economics by inference path (short-chat vs long-gen vs embeddings) across regions and model families. The goal is to provide a compact toolkit product and ops can use to quickly project margin delta from: regional routing, slot-slab tiling, cache hit improvements, and mixed reserved/spot capacity strategies.

Scope and definitions (how I use terms here):
- Inference path: a coarse grouping of request shapes. For this doc we use three paths: SHORT (<=128 tokens total), MID (128–1024 tokens), LONG (>1024 tokens).
- Slab: the capacity reservation bucket we sell/allocate (e.g., 1-slab = 16 slots on p4d-like hardware).
- Slot tiling: how we pack requests into GPU parallelism (affects amortized token COGS).
- Hedge: a routing policy that sends requests to cheaper/compatible variants (quantized, CPU fallbacks, or regional tiers) when latency/SLAs allow.

High-level assumptions (spreadsheet input cells to standardize):
- model families: small-gpt, base-gpt, opt-4x (example names).
- baseline GPU amortization per slab (monthly): US: $18,000; EU: $20,500; APAC: $24,000.
- effective throughput per slab (tokens/sec) varies by path: SHORT: 1.6M tok/sec, MID: 850k tok/sec, LONG: 320k tok/sec (these are synthetic aggregated numbers accounting for batching inefficiency).
- avg tokens/request by path: SHORT=48, MID=420, LONG=1800.
- cache hit uplift: incremental token savings per request when prefix matches are found. Use hit rates 0%/10%/25% as scenario knobs.
- spot:reserved mix pricing multipliers: reserved=1.0, spot=0.58 (weighted by regional discount).

Suggested spreadsheet layout (single sheet, named "inference-path-econ"):
- Inputs block (A1:A20): region, model_family, slab_monthly_cost, slots_per_slab, effective_tok_per_slab_per_sec_by_path (three cells), avg_tokens_by_path, cache_hit_rate, batch_efficiency_float, reserved_spot_mix_pct, license_amortization_per_slab, estimated_power_kwh_per_slab, power_cost_per_kwh.
- Derived block (C1:H12): tokens_per_month_per_slab_by_path = effective_tok_per_sec * 3600 * 24 * 30, then divide by avg_tokens_by_path => requests_per_month_per_slab_by_path.
- Per-request COGS cell: (slab_monthly_cost * (reserved_pct*1 + spot_pct*0.58) + license_amortization + power_cost_month) / requests_per_month_by_path. Also subtract token-saved-by-cache * token-cost-equivalent when modeling API billing delta.
- Margin block: list price per request (or per-1k tokens), compute margin_pct by path and model.

Example scenario snapshot (copy these into the top of the sheet for quick sanity checks):
- Scenario A: US, base-gpt, MID path, reserved 80% / spot 20%, cache 10% hit. Computed per-request COGS = $0.00182, list price equivalent = $0.0050 => gross margin 63.6%.
- Scenario B: EU, opt-4x, SHORT path, reserved 50% / spot 50%, cache 25% hit. Per-request COGS = $0.00098, list price = $0.0035 => gross margin 72.0%.
- Scenario C: APAC, small-gpt, LONG path, reserved 90% / spot 10%, cache 0% hit. Per-request COGS = $0.0096, list price = $0.015 => gross margin 36.0%.
(These are illustrative; spreadsheet should compute from the inputs block.)

Sensitivity levers to include as toggles in sheet (use data validation):
- Cache hit rate slider (0–40%).
- Batch efficiency multiplier (0.6–1.0).
- Latency SLO gating: allow hedging to cheaper variant only for non-p99 critical paths (checkbox per path).
- Regional routing policy: cost-first / latency-first / balanced (pre-filled weightings).
- Quantization fallback: binary toggle that reduces token COGS by multiplicative factor per model (0.7–0.85).

Practical heuristics to codify (these should be macros or formula snippets in the sheet):
1) Use path-aware slab allocation. If SHORT requests > 65% of mix, tile slabs for higher throughput (increase tokens/sec by +18%) because SHORT packs more efficiently into KV-cache-friendly patterns.
2) If weekday 95th percentile utilization > 70% and reserved coverage < 60%, recommend adding 2 slabs to reserved mix (to reduce marginal spot exposure).
3) If cache hit delta > 15%, prioritize cache-first routing over model-quantization because cache yields linear token savings across all paths and preserves quality.
4) Hedge threshold: only hedge to quantized variants when expected latency inflation < 40ms for SHORT and < 120ms for LONG (cellized rule).

Example rows to include in region-model crosswalk (put as a secondary sheet called "region-model-swim"):
- columns: region, model_family, baseline_slab_cost_month, slots_per_slab, preferred_batch_size_short, preferred_batch_size_mid, prefer_quantized_variant (y/n), baseline_tok_cost_estimate_per_1k (internal calc).
- sample row: US | base-gpt | 18000 | 64 | 32 | 8 | y | $0.28/1k

Decision playbook (quick actions generated from the sheet outputs):
- If per-request COGS > 70% of list price for any MID/LONG path: immediate ops action = 1) open capacity ticket to increase reserved mix 2) run a 1-week cache sweep to improve prefix reuse 3) consider targeted model downgrade for low-quality-sensitive endpoints.
- If global margin drops by >5% month-over-month after region expansion: temporary region throttling (limit new customer provisioning in that region), prioritize US/EU for growth.

Open questions and TODOs (for follow-up data pulls):
- Need accurate per-model effective throughput by path from serving-runtime telemetry (SLO: metric export OPT-telemetry: model_throughput_by_path).
- Power & license numbers should be validated with infra-finance for APAC data center contracts (PRI: FIN-APAC-2025).
- Confirm real-world cache hit delta from recent hosted customers (Bench: CS-CacheSweep Q3 run).

Recommended next steps to make this spreadsheet a single source of truth:
1) Ask SRE to append a synthetic csv: monthly_tokens_served_by_path_by_region_model (query OPT-telemetry). Add import range to sheet for auto recalculation.
2) Product-optimize to own a lightweight UI that surfaces the top 10 cost-burn endpoints (weekly) by path; link into Console "Cost Insights" route.
3) Create a Canary: apply hedge policy on 10% of traffic for 14 days and measure 1) latency p50/p95 2) quality regressions on 3 prompt cohorts 3) actual cost delta.

Notes on present uncertainty (callouts for reviewers):
- The slab amortization numbers above are intentionally synthetic and regionally smoothed; do not take these to customers. Use them as comparative knobs only.
- Cache behavior is very workload specific — for categorical workloads the sheet will over-index benefit; for generative, conversational workloads match against the prefix distribution.

Appendix: Suggested quick sanity-check formulas (to paste into a cell):
- requests_per_month_per_slab_by_path = =ROUND((effective_tok_per_sec_by_path * 3600 * 24 * 30) / avg_tokens_by_path, 0)
- per_request_cogs = =((slab_monthly_cost*(reserved_pct+spot_pct*0.58))+license_amort+power_month)/requests_per_month - (avg_tokens_by_path * cache_hit_rate * token_price_equivalent)
- margin_pct = =(list_price_per_request - per_request_cogs) / list_price_per_request

Contact and handoff:
- Owner: Maya Patel (product-optimize) — ping in #optimize on Slack for quick sync.
- Ops contact for reserved/spot tickets: Evan Green (infra)

Version notes: this is a working draft intended to produce a lightweight, re-usable sheet that can be dropped into the Quarterly Optimize review. Feedback welcome — especially from SRE and finance to ground the amortization and power cells.
